verified_facts.text: A vast, dark ocean that could host life, reachable only through ice.
The governing physics: tidal flexing by Jupiter keeps a salty ocean liquid beneath Europa's ice shell.
Earth isn't the water world of the Solar System; Europa may hold more water than all our oceans.
Europa hides more water than all Earth's oceans.
It's under an icy shell on a moon of Jupiter.
Its ocean may be 2 to 3 times Earth's ocean volume.
The rigid top layer of ice may be as thin as 200 metres.
Plumes of water may erupt through cracks.
In 2022, Juno flew within 320 kilometres of it.
Reaching the water would still mean drilling through ice.
So the best place to look for life may be under ice, not on land.
This leads to a volume of Europa's oceans of 3×1018m3, between two or three times the volume of Earth's oceans.
Models suggest the outer elastic portion of the ice crust could be as thin as 200 metres (660 ft).
In May 2018, astronomers provided supporting evidence of water plume activity on Europa, based on data from the Galileo space probe.
In September 2022, the Juno spacecraft flew within around 320km (200 miles) of Europa.
Tidal flexing by Jupiter keeps a salty ocean liquid beneath Europa's ice shell.
